title: Acceptance Helix: priority allocator with soft fallbacks
creator: Maya Lin
description:
Problem: During regional capacity pressure and cross-region failover events we see sudden request spikes that push latency and p99 above SLOs for high-value customers. Existing admission controllers are monolithic and lack a graded, observable path to gracefully degrade requests without wholesale rate-limits.

Goal: Implement a new admission allocator (Acceptance Helix) that assigns incoming requests into rotating acceptance bands based on SLO priority, regional budget, request affinity, and realtime load signals. The allocator should provide soft fallbacks (progressive fidelity modes) rather than hard rejections: e.g., compressed payloads, shorter generation budgets, partial responses, or model variant fallback. The system must integrate with circuit breakers and multi-region failover logic and be operable by on-call via a concise runbook.

Scope: - Design and implement Helix allocator service + lightweight runtime hook in the gateway. - Support per-tenant SLO buckets, per-region acceptance credits with decay curves, and request affinity windows. - Expose metrics, dashboards, and tracing for debugging decisions. - Provide a canary rollout with experiment flags and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.

Out of scope: full model slimming instrumentation and long-term chargeback reporting (will follow as separate work).
acceptance_criteria: Allocator routes requests into at least 4 acceptance bands (gold, silver, bronze, degraded) with documented semantics for each band.
Soft-fallback behaviors implemented: compressed response option, generation-length cap, partial JSON output, and model-variant fallback for degraded band.
Per-tenant and per-region acceptance credits tracked and visible in Console with realtime burn rate charts.
Circuit breaker integration: when model pool enters high-error mode, allocator transitions eligible traffic to degraded band and emits alert.
Canary rollout: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automated SLO checks; rollback triggers within 15 minutes if p99 or error-rate thresholds breached.
Runbook written and validated by on-call with at least one tabletop exercise.
implementation_steps: Design: final spec doc and sequence diagrams (Confluence link in design_doc).
Prototype: in-gateway hook that applies simple acceptance bands based on tenant headers and config flags.
Service: implement Helix allocator (stateless control plane + sharded credit store) with Redis-backed short-lived credit buckets and decay policy.
Runtime integration: lightweight SDK in serving runtime to query allocator decisions and apply fallback transforms (token budget clamp, compression).
Observability: add metrics (acceptance_band,count; band_latency_histograms; band_error_rates; credit_burn_rate), traces linking decision -> model invocation.
Testing: load tests with synthetic multi-region failover scenarios, chaos tests for partial region outage, and correctness tests for credit decay math.
Rollout: feature-flagged canary, monitor SLO probes, promote on green or rollback on alarm.
observability: Dashboard: Acceptance Helix Overview (per-region and per-tenant filters) showing band distribution and burn rate.
SLO probes: p50/p95/p99 latency by band, error-rate by band, percent-requests-degraded.
Alerts: high degradation spike (>20% of gold->degraded in 5m), credit exhaustion for enterprise tenants, circuit-breaker open for a model pool.
Tracing: single request trace should show allocator decision span and fallbacks applied.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal QA with 1% traffic and synthetic failovers for 72h. Phase 2: canary to 10% for low-risk tenants (48h) + automated SLO checks. Phase 3: 50% progressive for mixed tenants (72h). Phase 4: full rollout. Immediate rollback criteria: p99 latency increase >20% for gold tenants or error-rate >0.5% absolute increase vs baseline.
notes: Design trade-offs: we prefer soft fallbacks to maintain user-visible continuity. Using short-lived credit buckets allows quick rollback and simple decay math but increases operational telemetry churn. We chose Redis for speed and TTL semantics; if telemetry volume is a problem we'll iterate with a streaming-credit approach.
tests: Load test scenarios: region-failover-2x, global-spike-5x, tenant-burst-1000rps.
Chaos scenarios: Redis partition, allocator instance restart, model-pool OOM.
Unit tests for credit decay math and band selection determinism.
